description: Evergreen tree of the talares, carrying small dark fruit packed directly along its branches. One of the steadiest bird feeders in rioplatense woodland. Older references use the name Rapanea laetevirens.
nativeStatus: Native to the Río de la Plata region
ecology: A core tree of the talares and riverside woodland. Being evergreen it holds cover right through winter, and it fruits heavily enough to carry frugivorous birds through the lean months.
wildlifeNotes: The dark fruits sit in tight clusters along the stems where birds can work them easily, and thrushes strip them. The dense evergreen crown doubles as cover and nest structure.
size: Altura / height: 6-10 m. Porte: árbol pequeño a mediano, perenne y denso.
flowering: Small greenish flowers clustered along the branches
fruiting: Dark purple fruit along the stems
sources: Fichas de plantas nativas, Aves Argentinas: https://www.avesargentinas.org.ar/plantas-nativas
